results.summary_before: This design contains analog and custom layout experiments, primarily a current-starved ring oscillator VCO and a DAC, with digital test outputs and VGA signals. The VCO frequency is controlled by an analog input voltage and can be monitored directly or through divided digital outputs. Testing requires a precision variable voltage source and an oscilloscope to observe oscillation and frequency changes. The documentation provides detailed test steps and expected behavior, indicating it is an experimental analog block for the TT GF analog shuttle.
results.summary: TinyQV is a small RISC-V SoC implementing the RV32EC instruction set plus the Zcb and Zicond extensions, with 28-bit addresses, 24-bit program addresses, and hardcoded gp and tp values. Instructions are read using QSPI from flash, and a QSPI PSRAM is used for memory, with the QSPI clock and data lines shared between flash and RAM so only one can be accessed at a time. Code can only be executed from flash, while data can be read from flash and RAM and written to RAM, and many peripherals are contributed by the Tiny Tapeout community. This version also includes Matt Venn's R2R DAC as an additional peripheral, and the design is intended to be used with a QSPI PMOD and the RP2040 on the demo board.
